field_notes.attack_power / guarded_damage_negation /: Base values at +0 (Standard affinity) from the page infobox. Scaling grades: S > A > B > C > D > E, null = no scaling.
field_notes.skill.fp_cost: Wiki notation 'X (Y Z)': X = FP cost of the skill itself, Y/Z = FP cost of the light/heavy follow-ups. '-' = none.
field_notes.skill.type: 'Unique Skill' = exclusive skill (never sold as an Ash of War); 'Ash of War skill' = an 'Ash of War: <name>' item exists on the wiki; 'Standard skill (no Ash of War item)' = non-unique skill with no Ash of War item.
field_notes.passive_effects / status_buildup: Innate on-hit effects at +0 (status buildup values grow with upgrades for some weapons).
field_notes.upgrade.material: Smithing Stones => max +25; Somber Smithing Stones => max +10 and the weapon cannot take Ashes of War. null = the wiki page does not document it.
field_notes.upgrade.*_info_source: Where the value comes from: 'wiki (...)' = stated on the weapon page (template, text or upgrade table); 'deduced (...)' / 'game rule (...)' = strict logical consequence of what the page states. 'wiki (Armaments by Bolstering Material)' / 'wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments)' = row of the wiki list pages of the same names (one row per armament).
field_notes.upgrade.estimate_if_undocumented: Only present when the wiki page does not document the upgrade path AND the documented examples of the same group (unique skill / other skill / catalyst) support at least medium confidence: statistical guess with its basis. Treat as unverified.
field_notes.upgrade.ash_of_war_changeable / affinity: true/false only when stated by the wiki (or implied by somber material); null = not documented.
field_notes.upgrade.tables: Per-affinity reinforcement data when the page provides it (levels '+N'; 'growth_per_level' = % growth per level as shown on the wiki). Scaling values: grade + coefficient when available. Coverage varies between pages.
field_notes.upgrade.tables_consistent_with_infobox: false = the page's upgrade table +0 physical attack differs from the infobox (wiki data inconsistency, prefer the infobox).
field_notes.regions_mentioned: Map regions detected in the acquisition text (helper for game-progression analysis).
field_notes.acquisition_flags: Heuristic tags derived from the acquisition text.
field_notes.notes / acquisition.details: Bullet text from the wiki; nested bullets are prefixed with '→' (one per nesting level).
field_notes.description / skill.description: English in-game descriptions (weapon page / skill page).
field_notes.skill.stamina_cost_wiki: Same 'X (Y Z)' notation as fp_cost, from the skill page.
field_notes.upgrade.buffable: Only present when the wiki states whether the weapon can be buffed (grease/spells).
field_notes.patch_notes: Balance changes listed on the weapon page: game version, official patch note, community explanation.
field_notes.compatible_ashes_of_war: Only on the few pages that list them.
field_notes.range: Bow/crossbow/ballista range as shown in the infobox (in-game 'Range' value).
field_notes.sorcery_scaling / incantation_scaling: Catalysts: base spell power at +0 from the infobox (Sorcery Scaling for staves, Incantation Scaling for seals).
field_notes.upgrade.tables.*.spell_buff: Catalysts: sorcery/incantation scaling at that upgrade level ('?' on the wiki => omitted).
field_notes.material_inconsistencies_flagged: Weapons whose upgrade.material, read from a wiki list page ('Armaments by Bolstering Material'), is contradicted by another statement on the weapon's own page. Each item: name, reason, url. The list value is kept in upgrade.material and the weapon is reported in derived.inconsistent as 'upgrade.material'. Distinct from wiki_inconsistencies_flagged, which only names weapons whose upgrade table contradicts the infobox (see tables_consistent_with_infobox). Carian Sorcery Sword: material comes from the list page 'Armaments by Bolstering Material' (Somberstone, max +10), but the weapon page also says 'At +25 it has 163 Sorcery Scaling' and a patch note quotes a +25 value, which implies regular Smithing Stones; the list value is kept.

material_inconsistencies_flagged.name: Carian Sorcery Sword
material_inconsistencies_flagged.reason: upgrade.material comes from the list page 'Armaments by Bolstering Material' (Somberstone, max +10), but the weapon page also says 'At +25 it has 163 Sorcery Scaling' and a patch note quotes a +25 value, which implies regular Smithing Stones; the list value is kept.

weapons.name: Dagger

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
A standard dagger with a straight blade.

Though modest in reach and capacity for harm, this weapon is light enough to jab in rapid succession and delivers devastating critical hits.

details: 1 sold by the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold for 400 Runes.

A base 4% chance to drop from drop dagger-wielding enemies (Highwaymen, Godrick Foot Soldiers, Raya Lucaria Foot Soldiers, Radahn Foot Soldiers, Leyndell Foot Soldiers, Haligtree Foot Soldiers, and Messmer Foot Soldiers).
→ A good early farming spot is all the Highwaymen at the beginning of Murkwater Cave.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Together with the Rapier this weapon has the second strongest critical multiplier at 130 (the Miséricorde has the highest, at 140).

Has low enough requirements to be used with any starting class's default attributes and is fairly common, making it a decent secondary weapon for backstabbing and other critical hits, especially for those who don't have the stats to wield the Miséricorde.

Generally Dexterity-leaning on its affinities and performs best on a Keen affinity (having scaling just short of S-tier scaling) but also works surprisingly well with the Occult affinity, even if it lacks any of the innate Status Effects required to truly take advantage of this.

→ Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
The shortest of all daggers.

weapons.name: Parrying Dagger

skill.name: Parry
skill.description: Use this skill in time with a foe's melee attack to deflect it and break that foe's stance. This provides an opening to perform a critical hit.

weapons.description:
A knife with curved handguards. Designed to parry, turning foes' attacks against them.

For masters of combat who anticipate every enemy strike and counter accordingly, this weapon is all they need.

details: 1 can be bought from Patches for 1,600 Runes in any of his locations (Murkwater Cave is the earliest).

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
The second strongest of all the regular non-Wakizashi daggers on a Keen or Quality affinity, after the Celebrant's Sickle and Bloodstained Dagger respectively.

→ Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
→ Otherwise pretty mediocre damage-wise, with a leaning towards Dexterity on most of its affinities.

Having Parry as its skill gives early access to Parrying without having to buy Ash of War: Parry from Knight Bernahl or venture out of Limgrave and the Weeping Peninsula. It is however outclassed slightly by any Small Shield with the skill, especially the also-available-early Buckler.
→ Decent off-hand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield daggers.

weapons.name: Miséricorde

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Dagger favored by military physicians in white. The pointed blade is hard and sharp, making critical hits especially potent.

Medicine is mercy, and mercy upon the battlefield is ruthless. Beware the killers clothed as men of compassion.

details: Looted off a corpse that's only accessible behind a fog wall that requires 1 Stonesword Key to open. The fog wall is near the roaming Grafted Scion inside Stormveil Castle and the elevator shortcut back up to the Rampart Tower Site of Grace.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Has the highest critical multiplier in the game, at 140.

Generally average or above average damage depending on the affinity used, but always the strongest dagger for Critical Attacks such as backstabbing or riposting. As such it's useful as a secondary weapon to be pulled out quickly, even when a build isn't focused on daggers.
→ Deals damage equivalent to a Colossal Weapon, for comparison.

→ This damage is strong enough that a riposte with a Fire affinity Miséricorde can oftentimes overwhelm the flat defences that often hold back split damage weapons, dealing strong damage (doesn't work as well on backstabs since the damage multiplier for them is lower).
While it technically leans towards Dexterity it actually performs about as well on the Heavy affinity as the Keen affinity, technically better due to most daggers not working as well with Strength.

→ Actually the strongest pure Dexterity dagger with the Cold affinity and the strongest dagger period on the Occult affinity, but lacks the support of other Status Effects that other daggers such as the Bloodstained Dagger and Great Knife have.

→ Despite the general Dexterity tendency its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Main-gauche Shadow of the Erdtree, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
Somewhat stronger on lower stats than other daggers due to its higher base damage but lower scaling.
The longest of all daggers.

weapons.name: Great Knife

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Large knife with a broad, curved blade.

This weapon is designed to slash and rend, inflicting blood loss upon the recipient.

details: Starting equipment for the Bandit class.
2% drop chance from Small Demi-Humans.
→ The earliest farming spot is just inside Lakeside Crystal Cave, where one can be found hiding inside of a bush next to a regular Demi-Human.
→ The most efficient farming spot is just north of the Craftsman's Shack Site of Grace on Mt. Gelmir, where four of them are hiding amongst a flock of Sheep.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Leans more towards the various Dexterity- and Arcane-scaling affinities.
→ Pairs well with the similarly Dex/Arc-leaning Reduvia as an off-hand weapon for dual wielding.
→ Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.

→ Its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
→ While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
Curiously, the Strength-scaling of the Keen affinity is actually stronger than that of the Standard affinity, despite the Keen affinity usually greatly decreasing the Strength-scaling of the weapon.
On the shorter side of daggers.

weapons.name: Bloodstained Dagger

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Dagger with a bloodstained blade. Afflicts targets with blood loss.

As blood darkened the dagger through repeated slashing and stabbing, its blade only grew sharper and harder.

details: 2% drop rate from Fierce Demi-Humans aka Demi-Human Chiefs.
→ One can be found asleep next to the bridge west of the South of the Lookout Tower Site of Grace.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Strong Strength- and Arcane-scaling.
→ Surpasses all daggers except the rather unusual Wakizashi for raw damage on a Heavy affinity and has the highest Strength-scaling of them all, just short of an S-rating.
→ Second or third strongest dagger on the Occult affinity, though it will only slightly outmatch the Reduvia (only by 1 point) and the latter will have more Blood Loss build-up.
→ Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.

→ Despite this its Heavy affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
→ While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
The only dagger with a Strength focus on its Cold affinity instead of a Dexterity focus.

weapons.name: Erdsteel Dagger

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
An erdsteel dagger with a grass crest engraved upon its blade. Carried by the Erdtree royalty for self-defense in times of peace.

Though forged to a high standard, the weapon is difficult to wield. Attack power also scales with faith.

details: Received from Kenneth Haight after helping him retake Fort Haight.

Can be found in Leyndell, Royal Capital in the sewer area under the wing of Gransax near a fire-spitting Gargoyle Statue. From the Avenue Balcony Site of Grace, proceed northwest along the avenue and drop down in the pit to the far left.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Extremely good on the Faith-scaling Flame Art and Sacred affinities and below average on the rest. Can have an over 100 point lead in Attack Power compared to other affinities.

→ Since the Faith-scaling by default applies to the Physical damage for all affinities, these two affinities allow for double-dipping for damage, even more so if stacked with the flat damage bonuses from Flaming Strike and Sacred Blade.
→ The double-dipping effectively pulls it B-scaling on Faith-scaling affinities to the equivalent of an S-scaling.
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
→ This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.

→ In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities is only shared with the Clayman's Harpoon while the DLC adds the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, Fire Knight's Greatsword, and Fire Knight's Shortsword, weapons which all have the same quality.
Due to a bug this weapon actually doesn't have an actual Arcane-scaling on Poison, Blood, and Occult affinities.

weapons.name: Fire Knight's Shortsword
weapons.japanese_name: 火の騎士の短剣 (Hi no Kishi no Tanken)

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Shortsword used by the Fire Knights. A slender blade that undulates like fire.

Blessed with a flame incantation. Further flame imbuement will amplify the effect and greatly increase the armament's power.

details: Dropped by dual dagger-wielding Fire Knights with a 4% droprate.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Generally leans towards Dexterity-scaling over Strength-scaling.

Despite the description this dagger actually has higher Faith-scaling and raw Attack Power (AP) on a Sacred affinity than on a Flame Art affinity. It's also outclassed in raw AP by a Flame Art affinity Erdsteel Dagger.

→ However, the Fire Knight's Shortsword's Flame Art affinity usually has higher effective damage than the Sacred affinity due to only having to bypass 2 flat defences rather than 3, and the Fire damage will be higher on its own than either the Sacred affinity's Holy damage or the Flame Art Erdsteel Dagger's Fire damage.
Surprisingly enough, since this weapon is themed after Faith and Fire, it actually has the strongest Intelligence-scaling of all Daggers on the Magic and Cold affinities.
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger.
→ This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.

Though the innate Fire damage is low on all but the Fire and Flame Art affinities, simply having it means it will immediate reset fully applied Frostbite on the next hit if using Frostbite-causing skills such as Chilling Mist. It will also stun enemies that are extremely vulnerable to fire, such as Fingercreepers and Miranda Sprouts and Blossoms.

→ There is a bug, where using the Magic, Cold, Lightning, or Sacred Affinities with this weapon prevents the usual on-hit effect from dealing Fire damage from taking place. This means that using any of those Affinities means that the weapon won't stun Fingercreepers, won't detonate red barrels, and won't remove fully applied Frostbite from targets.
→→ This also applies to the Fire Knight's Greatsword and Queelign's Greatsword.
If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.

→ In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities was only held by the Clayman's Harpoon and the Erdsteel Dagger, while the DLC added the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, and Fire Knight's Greatsword, weapons which all have the same quality.

weapons.name: Wakizashi

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Short sword with a tempering pattern on the blade. A weapon unique to warriors of the Land of the Reeds. Afflicts targets with blood loss.

These swords are considered auxiliary weapons. Yet, one man is known to wield this weapon in his left hand while using a full-sized katana in his right. A demonic swordman known only as Okina.

details: Found on a corpse inside a locked cell in Gaol Cave, located in Caelid. The cave requires one Stonesword Key to access.
From the lever that unlocks all the cages it can be found by taking a right then a left, and then it's one of three items in the second cage on the left.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Overall is slightly stronger on Dexterity-scaling affinities.
Counts as a Katana for the purpose of dual wielding and as such cannot be paired with another dagger except for a second copy of itself.
→ Its attacks deal 15-28% more damage when dual wielded with a Katana in the right-hand slot and dual wield attacks cost 20% less Stamina, at the cost of bad reach.
→ Useful for granting access to the skill Parry when dual wielding Katanas.
→ Also uses the Katana dual wield moveset when wielded alongside another Wakizashi, though this will not cause the damage increase for the Wakizashi in the left-hand slot.

Consistently the strongest dagger damage-wise for all affinities despite its often only average scaling, in large part due to its high base damage. However, it effectively lacks access to the powerful Daggers dual wield moveset and the one for Katanas is much slower and as such will have much worse status build-up.

The innate Blood Loss build-up pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
→ While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.

weapons.name: Main-gauche

skill.name: Parry
skill.description: Use this skill in time with a foe's melee attack to deflect it and break that foe's stance. This provides an opening to perform a critical hit.

weapons.description:
Dagger with a large hand guard.

Intended to be used in the left hand, thereby complementing a piercing sword or identical blade held in the right to enable a distinctive style of fighting.

details: Found inside of Shadow Keep. From the Main Gate Plaza Site of Grace, head up the western stairs and take a right after the first stair, then take a right again in the corridor to arrive in a small room with a Black Knight. The dagger can be found on a body in the left corner.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Though this is a dagger it counts as a Thrusting Sword when dual-wielding, meaning that except for another copy of itself it cannot be dual-wielded with another dagger.
→ Uses the Thrusting Sword dual-wielding moveset if paired with itself.
→ Keep in mind that the second dual wield attack will only use the right-hand weapon, and hits 3 times.
→ Does more than a dagger usually would when dual-wielded, but not enough to truly compete with an actual Thrusting Sword.
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Miséricorde, and the Scorpion's Stinger.

Compared to a Thrusting Sword with Parry equipped, this dagger will have the same amount of start-up frames and takes the same amount of time to complete but with twice as many active parry frames, with a slightly shorter recovery time to compensate.

→ Since only the Rapier and Rogier's Rapier have increased Critical Attack damage (130 and 110 respectively), having this weapon in the off-hand to another Thrusting Sword to then two-hand upon making an enemy vulnerable to a such an attack might increase such damage.

weapons.name: Celebrant's Sickle

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Sickle decorated with flowers and many-colored fabrics. Ceremonial tool used by dancers during the festivities of Dominula. Its attacks can slip through an enemy's guard.

Crafted from human bone. Grants trace amounts of runes on landing attacks.

details: 0.5% drop chance from the blue Dominula Dancers in Dominula, Windmill Village, located in the north of Altus Plateau.
→ Two of them are found a bit east of the Windmill Village Site of Grace.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Grants 10 Runes every time an enemy is hit.

The strongest dagger for the Keen affinity, with its A being just on the verge of an S-scaling. Otherwise somewhat subpar or average when it comes to damage, including the otherwise Dexterity-scaling Lightning and Cold affinities.

→ Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.

→ Pairs well with non-physical affinities such as Magic since those are usually already only partially negated by guarding and the ignored guarding damage negation applies to all forms of damage, not just Physical.

→ As a dagger its one-handed non-jumping attacks will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased guard penetration
patch_notes.community_notes: Increased the amount of ignored Guarded Damage Negation per attack from 40% to 50%. Also applied to a variety of other guard-piercing weapons.

weapons.name: Ivory Sickle

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
Sickle fashioned from ivory. Weapon carried by aged Albinaurics.

These weapons are evidence of their dedication to the Haligtree, despite never having entered its presence.

details: Found near the Village of the Albinaurics Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.

While the skill, Quickstep, is rather generic for an innate, locked skill, it's still very useful for quicker traversal on surfaces that slow you down, like deep muck or water, and for getting around in combat aggressively.

→ Due to this weapon's mild Intelligence requirement and light weight, it allows for exploiting the fact that Quickstep costs 0 FP if the weapon's requirements aren't met and 8 out of 10 Origins won't do so by default (only the Astrologer and Prisoner meet them). While this heavily limits the skill's in-combat usage (decreases amount of i-frames from 15 to 5) it does make it ideal for traveling over slowing surfaces.
Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
Though its Dexterity-scaling is slightly stronger than its Intelligence-scaling it gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence approach.
→ Though the description may give the impression that this is a Faith-scaling weapon, it has not association with that stat.

Overall a somewhat awkward weapon when it comes to how to best use it. A pure Intelligence build would do better with any other dagger with a Magic affinity while a hybrid Dex/Int build would probably prefer the Glintstone Kris.

→ It does admittedly serve as a decent stand-in for the aforementioned Glintstone Kris before getting it since it requires defeating two specific bosses holding Great Runes while the Ivory Sickle can be gained without defeating any boss at all if Stormveil Castle is bypassed and is available a bit earlier than most Cold or Magic affinity Skills. It's also a decent off-hand weapon but is somewhat hampered by requiring the somewhat hard-to-get-enough-of regular Smithing Stones.
All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low original Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
→ This applies to both the Physical damage and the Magic damage.

→ As a dagger its one-handed non-jumping attacks will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

weapons.name: Crystal Knife

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

weapons.description:
A knife made by sharpening hard crystal. Signature weapon of glintstone miners.

Used as tool to extract glintstone from broken rock, and as such a faint magic enwreathes the blade.

details: Found in a chest inside the Raya Lucaria Crystal Tunnel located in Liurnia of the Lakes. After taking the first elevator after the Site of Grace down and walking across a wooden beam it is inside the second room on the right, guarded by two distracted Marionette Soldiers.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.
Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
The scaling favors an equal split between Strength and Intelligence, with the higher Physical base damage making the Strength-scaling more equivalent to the technically higher Intelligence-scaling.
→ Surprisingly only 20 points/5% of total Attack Power behind when focused purely on Strength or Intelligence, or hybridizing Strength/Intelligence, Strength/Dexterity, or Dexterity/Intelligence.

Decent raw damage but the unusual, for a dagger anyway, lack of a critical multiplier means it ends up being outclassed by all of the other daggers, especially the Dagger and the Miséricorde, for the purpose of critical hits.
Pairs well with a Magic or Cold affinity Bloodstained Dagger due to it also scaling well with Strength.

weapons.name: Scorpion's Stinger

skill.name: Repeating Thrust
skill.description: Twist to build power, then unleash a flurry of thrusts.

weapons.description:
Dagger fashioned from a great scorpion's tail, glistening with scarlet rot.

A ceremonial tool used by heretics, crafted from the relic of a sealed outer god.

details: Found inside a chest near the Grand Cloister Site of Grace, located in the Lake of Rot. It inside the small shrine to the west that is guarded by a large group of Kindred of Rot.

notes: The Scorpion's Stinger cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Scorpion's Stinger cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.
The locked skill, Repeating Thrust, is somewhat useful for applying the weapon's innate Scarlet Rot though does notably lack the extra mobility from the usual Quickstep skill.
Scales quite well with Dexterity, enough to be neck-and-neck with the Parrying Dagger and the Celebrant's Sickle and to only be substantially surpassed by the Wakizashi.
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, Main-gauche, and the Miséricorde.
The Scarlet Rot build-up is flat; it does not increase no matter the stat investment or weapon upgrade level.

weapons.name: Cinquedea

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

passive_effects: Increases the damage of Bestial Incantations
weapons.description:
Short sword given to high ranking clergymen of Farum Azula. Raises potency of bestial incantations.

The design celebrates a beast's five fingers, symbolic of the intelligence once granted upon their kind.

details: On a body very far down at the cliff west of the Bestial Sanctum, on the same level as the Dragoncrest Shield Talisman. The Tarnished must carefully descend the cliffs by jumping onto roots, the domes of the pillars, and outcrops on the walls and pillars. Rainbow Stones can be used to help navigate safe descent.

notes: The Cinquedea cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Cinquedea cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.

+0.passive: Increases the damage of Bestial Incantations

+1.passive: Increases the damage of Bestial Incantations
