details: Dropped by the Valiant Gargoyles duo boss, along with the Gargoyle's Twinblade.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Generally the second strongest Greatsword on Strength-leaning Affinities, outmatched only by the longer Iron Greatsword.

→ Despite this strong affinity for Strength its Heavy affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
One of the shortest weapons in its Class, as with all Gargoyle weapons.
→ Despite this its one of the heavier weapons in its Class, with the Iron Greatsword being the only heavier infusable Greatsword at 12.0 units.
Above average Guard Boost and Physical blocking ability.

weapons.name: Gargoyle's Blackblade
weapons.japanese_name: ガーゴイルの黒剣 (Gāgoiru no Kokken)

skill.name: Corpse Wax Cutter
skill.description:
Lost skill of ancient heroes.

Lift the sword up high to release the power of corpse wax and launch it forwards as a blade-like projectile.

weapons.description:
Bronze greatsword wielded by Valiant Gargoyles, mended with blackened corpse wax. Deals holy damage.

Such is the mark of those who serve Maliketh, the Black Blade.

details: Dropped upon defeating the Black Blade Kindred outside of the Bestial Sanctum, along with the Gargoyle's Black Halberd.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Strongest on a hybrid Strength/Faith-build, followed by the slightly weaker pure Strength-build. A pure Faith-build, meanwhile, is about 4% weaker but is also outclassed by infusable weapons with the Sacred Affinity.

→ Do note that the projectile part of the skill scales with Faith, and as such the pure Faith build will have 8% more Attack Power than the hybrid build which in turn is 15% stronger than the pure Strength build.
The scaling of this weapon is rather weak, with a +10 Blackblade with minimum Attribute requirements having 85% the Attack Power of a +10 Blackblade with minimum Dexterity, 45 Strength, and 45 Faith.

weapons.name: Inseparable Sword
weapons.japanese_name: 分かたれぬ双児の剣 (Wakatarenu Sōji no Ken)

skill.name: Sacred Blade
skill.description: Grants armament's attacks holy essence and fires off a golden blade projectile. The armament retains its holy essence for awhile.
skill.attack_type: Holy and weapon's primary damage type

weapons.description:
Sword forged by compounding silver and gold. A sacred weapon to hunt Those Who Live in Death. Deals holy damage.

The inseparable twins found solace in the Golden Order, the only institution not to revile them as accursed beings.

details: Obtained after the death of D, Beholder of Death, meaning there are two ways to obtain this weapon.

→ The first way is the regular one, which is slower and require that the questlines of both D's and also Fia, Deathbed Companion, is completed, whereafter it is found where Fia sat in Deeproot Depths.

→ The second is to kill D, Hunter of the Dead (only possible during the first encounter with him, in Limgrave, and impossible thereafter) to obtain the Twinned Set from him and then give this armor to D, Beholder of Death in Siofra Aqueduct. This results in the second D becoming hostile at the spot where he was sitting after reloading the area, and killing him then awards the weapon (and the Twinned Set once more).

notes: Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones and cannot be buffed or infused.

Due to the strong Faith-scaling the projectile from its innate Sacred Blade skill is extremely strong, gaining up to 30% more Attack Power than when it's used on a weapon with Sacred Affinity and equivalent Faith levels.

Uses a unique, more vertical light-attack moveset derived from Dark Souls 2's Mirrah Greatsword and shared with the Banished Knight's Greatsword, Knight's Greatsword, and Leontiel's Greatsword Tarnished Pack.
One of the stronger Faith-based Greatswords, at the cost of needing a modest investment in Strength and Dexterity to wield.

Deals 20% bonus damage to Those Who Live in Death and prevents Skeletons from reviving. Combined with the extra 100% bonus damage when buffed with its innate Skill: Sacred Blade this results in ridiculous damage against such foes.
While it normally cannot be buffed it still gets the flat bonus damage after casting Sacred Blade.

weapons.name: Sword of Milos
weapons.japanese_name: ミエロスの剣 (Mierosu no Ken)

skill.name: Shriek of Milos
skill.description: Lets out a horrific cursed scream that reduces all damage negation and status resistances for nearby foes. While active, strong attacks will change to a combo attack.

weapons.description:
Sinister greatsword fashioned from a giant's backbone. The spines along each side of the blade have been tapered to a fine point and mete out wounds like a lopsided saw-blade.

Milos was undersized for a giant, and was viewed as sullied and terribly grotesque.

details: Can be acquired in two different, mutually exclusive ways:
→ Dropped by the Dung Eater when he invades in the southern end of the moat in Capital Outskirts, at the spot where Blackguard Big Boggart normally sits.
→ Alternatively also dropped by the Dung Eater if he is killed in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds before the invasion, along with the Omen Set.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The innate skill, Shriek of Milos, is essentially a variant of the Skill: Barbaric Roar which decreases the Damage Negation of nearby enemies upon activation.
→ Note that since the roar is a Power Shred debuff it doesn't stack with most other non-Frostbite Damage Negation debuffs (see the skill's page for more details).
→ Note that unlike the Sword of Milos's normal heavy attacks these attacks have roughly the same Stance damage as other Greatsword's charged heavy attacks, at the cost of being significantly slower.

→ Though it's possible to have this sword to use the skill to debuff enemies, if its only used for that it's generally more practical to carry other debuffing equipment such as the Winged Greathorn instead due to their usage being easier.
Has a unique underhand-slash heavy attack, shared with the Death's Poker.

→ The charged variant of this attack adds a short sprint before the attack. Note that this also means that it deals substantially less Stance damage than is usual, only 16.5 instead of the usual 33 (compare also with an uncharged heavy attacks 13.2 Stance damage).

This weapon benefits most from a hybrid Strength-Dexterity build, followed shortly by a pure Dexterity build and then by a pure Strength build. This is without accounting for the minor bonus to Strength-scaling the skill's Weapon Buff grants.

→ Some scaling examples: with 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity it gains 649 AP when one-handed and 691 AP when two-handed, with 15 Strength and 80 Dexterity it gains 650 Attack Power (AP) when one-handed and 673 AP when two-handed, and with 80 Strength and 19 Dexterity it gains 612 AP when one-handed and 637 AP when two-handed.
Note that though this weapon as innate Blood Loss build-up, the amount is relatively low and as such will usually only be inflicted once per fight against an elite enemy or a boss.
When the sword is held in an active hand, gain 5 FP when any nearby creature dies.
→ This doesn't stack if two Swords are held.
→→ Does stack with the Ancestral Spirit's Horn and Sacrificial Axe FP-gain-on-death effects.

→ As the killed creature doesn't have to be killed by the holder of the sword, or even be their enemy, having this sword is a boon to Invaders as they can simply retreat between combats and regain their FP by switching to this sword as the Host and Fingers kill regular enemies.

weapons.name: Marais Executioner's Sword
weapons.japanese_name: マレー家の執行剣 (Marē-ke no Shikkōken)

skill.name: Eochaid's Dancing Blade
skill.description: Infuse the sword with energy, then fling it forwards in a corkscrew attack. The sword continuously deals damage while violently spinning. Charge the attack to increase reach and duration of the spin.

weapons.description:
Storied sword of House Marais, the family of executioners who presided over the Shaded Castle. One of the legendary armaments.

Elemer of the Briar, the Bell Bearing Hunter, snatched the sword from the site of his looming execution, and furnished it with battle skills from his home of Eochaid.

details: Defeat Elemer of the Briar at the top of the castle.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The skill, Eochaid's Dancing Blade, is both chargeable (benefiting from the Godfrey Icon) and actually counts for repeated-hits boosters such as the Winged Sword Insignias and Thorny Cracked Tear, something many other repeated-hits skills such as the Ghiza's Wheel's skill Spinning Wheel or the Ornamental Straight Sword's skill Golden Tempering's special heavy attacks don't.

→ Since the skill's damage is based entirely of off the weapon's base Attack Power, and about a third of the Regalia's damage is Magic damage, Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear and Terra Magica functionally give +7% damage and +7.5% (+5% in PvP) damage respectively if they can be set up beforehand.

Though the Strength-scaling may appear to entirely outmatch the Arcane-scaling, the Arcane-scaling actually applies to BOTH the Physical damage and the Magic damage. This effectively places it as a high C-scaling (0.89 scaling instead of technical 0.54 scaling). Also, due to scaling falling off around 54 points in a damage stat (see the Weapon Scaling page) a hybrid Strength/Arcane build actually has slightly higher Attack Power than a pure Strength build.

→ For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Arcane grants 686 Attack Power (732 AP if two-handed), 67 Strength and 23 Arcane grants 679 AP (710 AP if two-handed), and 24 Strength and 66 Arcane grants 659 AP (695 AP if two-handed).
Has unique two-handed heavy attacks, which are overhead slams.
→ This attack has ever so slightly higher Attack Power multipliers than usual and are 0.4 seconds slower to use, whether charged or not.
→ Two-handed heavy attacks are always the same overhead slam.

weapons.name: Greatsword of Solitude

skill.name: Solitary Moon Slash
skill.description: Sharply slash downward using the greatsword, shooting forward an arc of light. Strong attack allows for an advancing follow-up.

weapons.description:
Steel greatsword wielded by the Knights of the Solitary Gaol.

Through a secret rite, they relinquished their hearts for heightened battle prowess. Next, they engraved their blades with two crests: one depicting the light of birth, and the other, solitude.

details: Dropped by the Knight of the Solitary Gaol found inside of the Western Nameless Mausoleum.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The innate skill, Solitary Moon Slash, is essentially the Skill: Storm Blade with a follow-up lunging attack.
Has extremely high Guard Boost and Physical block for a Greatsword, placing it more on par with a Colossal Sword or a weak Medium Shield.
Scales greatly with Strength, receiving only minimal benefits from Dexterity.

weapons.name: Leontiel's Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: レオティエルの大剣 (Reotieru no Daiken)

skill.name: Muleta
skill.description: Hold out a red cloth in front, inviting enemies to attack. Use normal or strong attack to gracefully dodge incoming attacks then pivot to offense. Can be charged to increase power of strong attack. Also, additional input allows for a follow-up attack.

weapons.description:
The knight Leontiel's favored weapon - a greatsword whose blade is wrapped in leather at the base.

Said to have been wielded by a proud order of orthodox knights long ago, weapons of this ilk demand high dexterity.

details: Received after defeating Knight Leontiel after she invades in the Wailing Dunes Tarnished Pack.
→ Starscourge Radahn must be defeated prior, then she will invade near the entrance to War-Dead Catacombs in the northern part of the area.

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Muleta is a unique stance skill that has the user hold up their Muleta in a provoking manner; performing a light attack dodges to the left with a horizontal slash, and performing a heavy attack dodges to the right for a chargeable thrust, an additional heavy input dodges to the right again for an upwards thrust that launches smaller enemies into the air.
→ The dodges with Muleta have i-frames.
→ All of the attacks of the skill deal Standard damage.
→ Godfrey Icon boosts the damage of Muleta's charged heavy attack.

Uses a unique, more vertical two-handed light attack moveset derived from Dark Souls 2's Mirrah Greatsword and shared with the Knight's Greatsword, Banished Knight's Greatsword, and the Inseparable Sword.
→ Shares unique thrusting heavy attacks with the Claymore, Lizard Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, and the Greatsword of Damnation Shadow of the Erdtree.
→ Also shares a unique thrusting rolling attack with the Claymore and the Greatsword of Damnation Shadow of the Erdtree.
This weapon makes fantastic use of the Rellana's Cameo Shadow of the Erdtree due to the skill's already high damage being boosted even further.

weapons.name: Ordovis's Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: オルドビスの大剣 (Orudobisu no Taiken)

skill.name: Ordovis's Vortex
skill.description: Channel the power of the crucible to spin the sword in midair, building momentum before slamming the blade down onto the ground. This skill can be charged to increase its power.

weapons.description:
Greatsword of Ordovis, one of the two honored as foremost among the Crucible Knights.

This sword is imbued with an ancient holy essence. Its red tint exemplifies the nature of primordial gold, said to be closer in nature to life itself.

details: Ordovis's Greatsword is received upon defeating the Crucible Knight Ordovis and Crucible Knight duo boss at the bottom of the Auriza Hero's Grave.

notes: Ordovis's Greatsword cannot be buffed or infused.
Ordovis's Greatsword can be upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.

Benefits mostly from Strength, with Dexterity offering almost no returns, and Faith providing mediocre amounts of Holy damage. This is especially true because the skill only scales with the weapon's Attack Power, rather than a secondary Attribute, as is usually the case.
As the skill is chargeable, the Godfrey Icon is useful for those who wish to maximize its increased damage and take advantage of the extra poise.
Both the skill and the weapon deal primarily Physical damage.

weapons.name: Alabaster Lord's Sword

skill.name: Alabaster Lords' Pull
skill.description: Thrust the armament into the ground to create a gravity well. In addition to dealing damage, this attack pulls enemies in. Has a greater area of effect than Gravitas.

weapons.description:
Greatsword forged from a blue-white meteoric ore. The blade conceals gravity-manipulating magic.

A weapon unique to the Alabaster Lords, a race of ancients with skin of stone who were said to have risen to life when a meteor struck long ago.

acquisition.location: Lake of Rot / Yelough Anix Tunnel
details: One each is dropped by respective the Alabaster Lord in the Lake of Rot and in Yelough Anix Tunnel.
→ Note that the sword will not drop if the Lord is killed at the same time as the player.

→ Lake of Rot one is reached by raising a series of platforms towards the end of the lake and then getting atop them by climbing up a cliff west of the entrance to the Grand Cloister to reach a gravitational anomaly.
→ The Lord in the Tunnel is found in a pit after the frozen elevator. Dropping down into the pit and turning around should make the anomaly the Lord is hiding in visible.

notes: The Alabaster Lord's Sword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
The Alabaster Lord's Sword cannot have its affinities changed with Ashes of War or Whetblades.
Deals an extra 20% damage against Gravity-type enemies.
The skill is essentially a stronger variant of the Skill: Gravitas, with 3 times as high base Attack Power and scaling somewhere between the Magic Affinity and Cold Affinity.
The shortest and lightest among all greatswords.

The 2-handed charged heavy attacks of this weapon deals damage on par with that of a Colossal Sword while draining much less Stamina than any other greatswords. 1-handed charge attacks have similar bonuses but much less of a damage increase.

→ To be precise, the 1-handed charged heavy attacks have a roughly 10% higher damage multiplier while the 2-handed charged heavy attack has a 34% damage multiplier, and both cost only 18 points of Stamina where the average stamina cost for greatswords for both is between 35 and 42 points of Stamina for the 1-handed ones and between 38 and 48 for 2-handed ones.

→ Every other charged heavy attack will also deal 33% more Stance damage, 44 insted of 33. Unlike other greatswords the heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks receive no bonus to Stance damage when two-handed.
Despite that being its highest Attribute requirement, its Intelligence scaling is rather subpar (even more so since the Magic Attack Power is so comparably low).

→ More precisely, only the Strength-scaling grants any notable increase in Attack Power when leveled (about 220 Attack Power when leveled to 80). Dexterity grants only about a third of the benefit (about 80 Attack Power when leveled to 80) and Intelligence only about a seventh (30 Attack Power when leveled to 80).
→ The skill has slightly stronger Intelligence-scaling, gaining 14% more Attack Power at 45 compared to 20 and 25% more Attack Power at 80 compared to 20.

weapons.name: Death's Poker

skill.name: Ghostflame Ignition
skill.description: Thrust out the barbed rod and set its tip alight with ghostflame. Follow up with a normal attack to set the ground ablaze with ghostflame, or a strong attack to trigger a massive explosion.

weapons.description:
Barbed rod carried by Deathbirds.

The birds are graveyard fire keepers; it is said they rake out the ashen remains of the dead from their kilns.

details: Dropped by the Death Rite Bird in Caelid, found southeast of the Southern Aeonia Swamp Bank Site of Grace at night.

→ The high cliff to the east of the boss can be used to cheese it, as it's rather bad at scaling the rocks. Combined with anti-Those Who Live in Death equipment and ranged attacks will kill it quickly.

→ It's also possible to lure the Bird off the southern cliffs since some of its attack have it jump in various directions, especially if its first lure to the southern cliffs and then pulled to a large branch to the east to keep it from moving around too much.

notes: Death's Poker is upgraded using Somber Smithing Stones.
Death's Poker cannot have its affinities altered using Ashes of War or Whetblades.
The innate skill, Ghostflame Ignition, is a strong, variable ranged or melee attack with considerable Frostbite build-up.
→ This skill is strong enough that the weapon can be primarily be used as a "staff" for it, being used for its exclusive "spell".
→ Unlike the weapon, it primarily scales with Intelligence (and weapon upgrade level) which provides something of a build conflict.
Has a unique underhand-slash heavy attack, shared with the Sword of Milos.

→ The charged variant of this attack adds a short sprint before the attack. Note that this also means that it deals substantially less Stance damage than is usual, only 16.5 instead of the usual 33 (compare also with an uncharged heavy attacks 13.2 Stance damage).

There is something of a conflict between the weapon's scaling and the skill's scaling, as the weapon scales best with Dexterity and quite well with Strength, but receives almost no benefit from Intelligence. Meanwhile, the only stat the skill scales with is Intelligence.
→ However, due to how weak the weapon's Intelligence-scaling is the skill receives only minimal benefits from it.

weapons.name: Helphen's Steeple
weapons.japanese_name: ヘルフェンの尖塔 (Herufen no Sentō)

skill.name: Ruinous Ghostflame
skill.description: Swing the sword to bathe its blade in ghostflame. The ghostflame adds magic damage to attacks, and also has a bitterly cold bite.

weapons.description:
Greatsword patterned after the black steeple of the Helphen, the lampwood which guides the dead of the spirit world.

The lamplight is similar to grace in appearance, only it is said that it can only be seen by those who met their death in battle.

details: Dropped by a Tibia Mariner in the Mountaintops, overlooking Castle Sol and not far from the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace and where you fight the Mountaintops' Death Rite Bird.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The unique skill functions as a very short-ranged melee attack, making it possible to buff or re-buff in the middle of an attack combo.
The weapon only has Frostbite build-up when buffed by the unique skill.

The Strength- and Intelligence-scalings are roughly equally strong, leading to a Strength/Intelligence hybrid build granting the most Attack Power, followed slightly by a pure Intelligence build and then by a pure Strength build.

weapons.name: Blasphemous Blade

skill.name: Taker's Flames
skill.description: Raise the sacred sword aloft to set it ablaze with blasphemous flames, then bring it down to fire off a forward blast. The flames steal HP from those they touch.

passive_effects: Restores HP equal to 4% of maximum HP + 40 upon nearby deaths
weapons.description:
Sacred sword of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. Remains of the countless heroes he has devoured writhe upon the surface of this blade.

Now they share the same blood, bound together as family. Some HP is restored upon defeating an enemy.

details: Trade the Remembrance of the Blasphemous, gained by defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, with Finger Reader Enia.
→ Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Note that the innate skill Taker's Flames, unlike the weapon, only scales with Faith through the Fire Attack Power of the weapon.
→ The skill also serves as the weapon's strongest attack, with roughly twice as much Attack Power as the weapon itself.
Restores HP equal to (4% of wielder's maximum HP + 40) if a nearby creature is killed while the sword is held in an active hand.
→ Effect stacks with Greathorn Hammer, Serpent-God's Curved Sword and Taker's Cameo.
→ This is in addition to the skill restoring HP equal to (10% of target's maximum HP + 150) upon hit.
Very heavy for a greatsword, being outweighed only by the Greatsword of Solitude.

Though the Faith-scaling is technically stronger than both its Strength- and Dexterity-scalings, as it scales with the lower Fire Attack Power instead of the higher Physical Attack Power it's effectively a very high D-scaling that is just ever so slightly lower than the other stats' very low C-scaling.

→ Overall, a hybrid Strength-Dexterity or Dexterity-Faith build gains the most Attack Power, while a pure Faith build sacrifices about 6% more weapon Attack Power in exchange for 12% more skill Attack Power.

weapons.name: Golden Order Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 黄金律の大剣 (Ōgonritsu no Taiken)

skill.name: Establish Order
skill.description: Raise the armament in salute, releasing a golden explosion. Repeated inputs send out waves of golden light.

passive_effects: +20% damage against Those Who Live in Death
weapons.description:
Greatsword made of light, modeled after the Elden Ring itself. Forged by the King Consort Radagon to proudly symbolize the tenets of the Golden Order. One of the legendary armaments.

Telltale signs betray that this was once the greatsword bequeathed to him by his first wife, Rennala.

details: Received upon defeating the Misbegotten Crusader at the end of the Cave of the Forlorn, located in the Consecrated Snowfield.

notes: This weapon is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
This weapon cannot be buffed or infused.
The innate skill, Establish Order, slowly unleashes a point-blank explosion with the initial skill use, and then spins twice to unleash a Holy wave with the follow-up skill use.
→ As most of the damage of the follow-up use comes from the second swing it has some surprise potential due to the first swing being far more limited and normal.

One problem with the weapon is that it's acquired at a point in the game where strongly Holy-resistant bosses are starting to become more common, which hurts its damage potential if using it to finish the game.
→ In Shadow of the Erdtree, enemies are generally far less resistant to Holy damage, making this less of a problem.

While a pure Faith build would be expected to be strongest investment in terms of pure Attack Rating (AR) for this weapon, after Faith reaches 50 Dexterity will grant roughly equal AR until it also reaches 50.

→ The first option will grant stronger casting, more damage from the skill and potentially also higher melee damage if an enemy has lower or equal Holy defence to its Physical defence. The second option grants slightly quicker casting and potentially slightly better damage if an enemy has higher Holy defence than Physical defence.

This is one of the few weapons that deal bonus damage (20% more specifically) to Those Who Live in Death enemies, such as Skeletons and Death Rite Birds, and will also prevent the former from resurrecting without needing an extra hit to finish them off.

weapons.name: Dark Moon Greatsword

skill.name: Moonlight Greatsword
skill.description: Raise the sword aloft, bathing it in the light of the dark moon. Temporarily increases magic attack power and imbues blade with frost. Charged attack release blasts of moonlight.

weapons.description:
A Moon Greatsword bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse to honor long-standing tradition. One of the legendary armaments.

Ranni's sigil is a full moon, cold and leaden, and this sword is but a beam of its light.

details: Found at the end of Lunar Princess Ranni's questline, in the spot where she sat underneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes, after giving her the Dark Moon Ring.

notes: The Dark Moon Greatsword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stone.
The Dark Moon Greatsword cannot have its affinities altered using Ashes of War or Whetblades.
The innate skill, Moonlight Greatsword, acts as a Weapon Buff to the weapon and also adds ranged projectiles to is regular and charged heavy attacks.

→ This skill is part of what makes the Dark Moon Greatsword such a strong weapon, as the added projectile attack is very strong in terms of both Attack Power and Stance damage, the Buff that grants it is fairly longlasting, and having an essentially free ranged attack helps keep up the pressure on tough targets.
Intelligence is by far the strongest scaling for this weapon, especially since it also strengthens the projectile part of the skill-buffed heavy attacks.
→ Unusually for a weapon with such a mediocre Strength-scaling, its skill is one of only a few that benefits from the Strength-boost granted by two-handing.

patch_notes.official_notes: Fixed a bug where the damage of some normal attacks of the Dark Moon Greatsword were lower than intended.
patch_notes.community_notes: The bug was that the second attack in the 4-part one-handed light attack chain had 68% weapon Attack Power instead of the usual 101% weapon Attack Power. The bug seems to have originally been introduced with either Patch 1.09 or Patch 1.09.1.

weapons.name: Greatsword of Damnation

skill.name: Golden Crux
skill.description: Leap up and skewer foe from overhead. If successful, the weapon's barbs unfold to excruciate from within; else, additional barbs in the area. There is something of the Golden Order in the sight of those fixed upon this crux.

weapons.description:
Golden greatsword that once pierced the body of Midra, master of the manse. Used by hornsent in the execution of a damnation like no other.

The barbs that pierce the victim from within wind gently around the blade.

details: Trade the Remembrance of the Lord of Frenzied Flame, gained by defeating Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame, with Finger Reader Enia.
→ Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki rule (Ashes of War cannot be applied to weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones)

notes: It's innate skill, Golden Crux, is effectively a jumping heavy attack with a follow-up explosion, that can also function as a grab if the initial attack hits another Tarnished.

Its one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, and two-handed rolling attacks and crouching attacks consist of a thrust instead of the usual slam, making this weapon much more compatible with the Spear Talisman than other Greatswords and granting it slightly more range with these attacks.
→ This trait is shared with the Claymore and Leontiel's Greatsword Tarnished Pack.

Strength provides the strongest scaling for the weapon's Attack Power, though as its scaling gains diminishing returns after 50 it becomes possible to gain roughly equal Attack Power by investing in Dexterity or Faith as it's with Strength beyond that point.

→ Investing in Strength or Dexterity makes it easier to benefits from the Counter Hits from the unique attacks and the skill, while investing in Faith gives access to more Incantations for offensive and defensive Buffs as well as attack spells.
Despite how Midra uses it in the fight against him, the Greatsword of Damnation does not inflict Madness.

weapons.name: Sacred Relic Sword

skill.name: Wave of Gold
skill.description: Imbue the sword with bygone golden glory, then fire it at foes. A wide, golden wave fans out forwards, sweeping through all enemies caught in its path.

weapons.description:
Sword wrought from the remains of a god who should have lived a life eternal.

Thoughts on what the weapon portends are many and varied. Some consider it the mark of a great sin, or a sign of a great devastation. Some think it as the end of an age, while others; the beginning.

details: Trade the Elden Remembrance, gained by defeating the Elden Beast, with Finger Reader Enia.
→ Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Its innate skill, Wave of Gold, is a somewhat slow but very wide and pretty long-range attack that is very hard to dodge without a roll.

→ Its long-lasting nature does make it somewhat vulnerable to desyncing making its visual model and its hitbox becoming quite disconnected if there are any problems in connection between a Host of Fingers and an Invader.
Despite its golden, holy appearance it scales by far the best with Dexterity, with both Strength and Faith providing more moderate benefits to the weapon's Attack Power.

→ While both a Strength-Dexterity hybrid build and a Dexterity-Faith hybrid build gains slightly less Attack Power compared to a pure Dexterity build, a Dexterity-Faith hybrid build does gain the benefit of higher Attack Power for the skill and access to supportive and defensive Incantations.

Surprisingly compatible with Sword of Milos, another weapon that also scales well with Dexterity for easy dual-wield compatibility and also replenishes a small amount of FP per kill, letting the skill be used more often without using the Flask of Cerulean Tears.
This is one of only two Greatswords with a boost to Critical Attacks, along with the Lordsworn's Greatsword.

weapons.name: Zweihander

skill.name: Stamp (Upward Cut)
skill.description: Brace armament and step into a low stance that prevents recoil from most enemy attacks. Follow up with a strong attack for an upward strike.

weapons.description:
Just about the largest sword a mere man is capable of swinging. True to its name, it is designed to be wielded in both hands, but those of merely ordinary strength will still struggle to do so.

The long blade is heavy and sharp, sending foes reeling back with its broader strokes, while also capable of a devastating piercing thrust.

details: One is sold for 3,500 Runes by the Isolated Merchant at the Isolated Merchant's Shack at the westernmost point of the Peninsula.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack in each two-attack chain is replaced by a thrust. This trait is shared with the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Moonrithyll's Knight Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, and Troll Knight's Sword.
→ This gives the weapon the versatility of having a thrust attack besides the crouching light attack.
Lightest Colossal Sword in the game.
→ This makes this weapon useful for dual-wielding.
The third longest Colossal Sword, after the Greatsword and the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword.
Leans towards Dexterity for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.
The Vagabond origin can wield this weapon two-handed without any additional levels.
→ For other origins and two-handing this weapon, Heroes need 2 more points in Dexterity and Confessors and Samurai need 1 more point in Strength.
Due to the relatively low wielding requirements and weight, this weapon is the infusable Colossal Sword that is most easily used for build that want to use non-Heavy, non-Fire Affinities.

→ It's also still fairly useful for those wishing to use either of those two Affinities, as the aforementioned advantages and early accessibility means that stat points can be focused on increasing other stats such as Vigor for more HP and Endurance for better armor, until the higher Attack Power of other Colossal Swords become more advantageous.
Low overall Attack Power on most non-Dexterity Affinities.

weapons.name: Greatsword

skill.name: Stamp (Upward Cut)
skill.description: Brace armament and step into a low stance that prevents recoil from most enemy attacks. Follow up with a strong attack for an upward strike.

weapons.description:
A coarse iron lump of an ultra greatsword. Mows down foes by utilizing its incredible weight.

Though handling it likely requires the wielder to have surpassed the realm of the merely human, it is precisely for this reason the weapon is used to slaughter even inhuman foes.

details: The found in a chest on the backside of a Carriage beside the road heading northwest from Caelem Ruins.
→ The location is southwest of the Minor Erdtree in Caelid and the Minor Erdtree Catacombs.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Has the generally highest Attack Power of all infusable Colossal Swords.
→ It's only slightly trailed by the Watchdog's Greatsword in terms of Attack Power, and the Zweihander's much lower Attribute requirements and weight makes it more suitable to non-Strength builds.
The second longest Colossal Sword, surpassed only by the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree.
Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack is a horisontal sweep and the second is an overhead slam.
Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.

→ Despite having the highest damage and scaling on its Heavy affinity it actually gives slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Vacuum Slice, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).

weapons.name: Watchdog's Greatsword

skill.name: Stamp (Upward Cut)
skill.description: Brace armament and step into a low stance that prevents recoil from most enemy attacks. Follow up with a strong attack for an upward strike.

weapons.description:
Stone greatsword wielded by Erdtree Burial Watchdogs.

Though decorated with the watchman's eye, the pupil was taken by graverobbers and is now hollow, leaving this sword a mere lump of stone.

acquisition.location: Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave / Giants' Mountaintop Catacombs (Mountaintops of the Giants) / Consecrated Snowfield Catacombs (Consecrated Snowfield)
details: 8% drop chance from the non-boss variant of Erdtree Burial Watchdog.

→ Most easily farmed in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave, by heading out the southwestern exit from the Site of Grace and then jumping out one of the windows to the right. After killing the two shaded Imps next to the Erdtree seal the Watchdog can be easily lured over to de-shade it and then be killed.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Has fairly good Attack Power, usually only trailing the Greatsword slightly.
Of middling length among its Weapon Class.
This is the only non-DLC, farmable infusable Colossal Sword.
Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.

→ Despite having the highest damage and scaling on its Heavy affinity it actually gives slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Vacuum Slice, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).

weapons.name: Fire Knight's Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 火の騎士の大剣 (Hi no Kishi no Taiken)

skill.name: Stamp (Upward Cut)
skill.description: Brace armament and step into a low stance that prevents recoil from most enemy attacks. Follow up with a strong attack for an upward strike.

weapons.description:
Greatsword of the Fire Knights. A long, slender blade that undulates like fire.

Blessed with a flame incantation. Further flame imbuement will amplify the effect and greatly increase the armament's power.

acquisition.location: Shadow Keep, Church District / Specimen Storehouse
details: 4% drop chance from greatsword-wielding Fire Knights.

→ One such knight can be found just before the elevator leading up to the Storehouse, First Floor Site of Grace. If the elevator is taken from the Grace the knight will start with its back turned, making it easier to defeat.

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 75 of 92 wiki-documented weapons with a non-unique skill use regular Smithing Stones

notes: As the description states, though the total Attack Power with the Flame Art Affinity is about on par with other Colossal Swords the distribution is different, with the Fire Attack Power making up about 70% of the total Attack Power instead of the usual 55%.

→ It also notably has the highest Holy Attack Power with the Sacred Affinity, though the also high total Attack Power is somewhat misleading since it includes its there-mediocre Fire Attack Power which will be harshly affected by enemy Defence.

→ This benefit is also there with the Fire Affinity, if with a much weaker benefit: the total Attack Power, though good, isn't higher than other Colossal Swords and the distribution difference is only 55% compared to total Attack Power whereas the other weapons in its Class usually have about 50% of the total Attack Power.

Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack in each two-attack chain is replaced by a thrust. This trait is shared with the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Moonrithyll's Knight Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, Troll Knight's Sword, and Zweihander.
→ This gives the weapon the versatility of having a thrust attack besides the crouching light attack.
Has unique one- and two-handed light attacks, which are more sweeping. This trait is shared with the Godslayer's Greatsword.
→ These attacks grant much more progress towards the Winged Sword Insignias' damage buff, giving 14 points per hit instead of the usual 8 per hit.

→ The first two attacks in both the one-handed and two-handed attack chains inflict less stagger on enemies, staggering for only about 75% of the time a Colossal Sword's light attack would normally and placing it on par with a Greatsword. Stance damage is not affected.
Fairly good reach, about on par with the Zweihander.

There is a bug, where using the Magic, Cold, Lightning, or Sacred Affinities with this weapon prevents the usual on-hit effect from dealing Fire damage from taking place. This means that using any of those Affinities means that the weapon won't stun Fingercreepers, won't detonate red barrels, and won't remove fully applied Frostbite from targets.
→ This also applies to the Fire Knight's Shortsword and Queelign's Greatsword.
Leans towards Dexterity for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.

patch_notes.official_notes: Fixed a bug where the damage animation of some attacks of the Fire Knight's Greatsword against players was different than expected.
patch_notes.community_notes: Lowered the damage level of the light attacks from 3 to 2 for the first two hits, putting it in line with the Godslayer's Greatsword. This removed the true combo for its light attacks, where hitting with one would stun an enemy players long enough to be hit with the second, which is normally not possible with Colossal Swords.

weapons.name: Troll's Golden Sword
weapons.japanese_name: トロルの黄金剣 (Tororu no Ōgonken)

skill.name: Troll's Roar
skill.description: Look into the distance and let out an intense roar, generating a powerful shockwave that blows back surrounding foes. Follow up with a strong attack to slam the armament down.
skill.attack_type: Strike, Standard and Weapon's Primary Damage Type

weapons.description:
Sword given to the lesser giants who fought for the Erdtree during the War against the Giants long ago.

Though the giants have lost their minds, they stay inseparable from their swords that are in sad shape—such that the gold plating had flaked away.

details: Found in a chest in the back of a Carriage in a Leyndell Soldier camp in-between the Erdtree-Gazing Hill and Altus Highway Junction Sites of Graces.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Essentially a slightly weaker and lighter version of the Watchdog's Greatsword that is also acquirable much earlier.
→ It's also the earliest Colossal Swords with non-unique heavy attacks.
This is the only infusable weapon with the Skill: Troll's Roar innately, making it a decent earlier weapon before getting the Ash of War for the skill in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

→ However, as the Troll Knight's Sword, the arguably strongest carrier of the skill (much stronger if the Golden Sword isn't infused with Heavy Affinity), is available even earlier than that this is a dubious advantage.
Mediocre length.
Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.

weapons.name: Troll Knight's Sword
weapons.japanese_name: トロルの騎士剣 (Tororu no Kishiken)

skill.name: Troll's Roar
skill.description: Look into the distance and let out an intense roar, generating a powerful shockwave that blows back surrounding foes. Follow up with a strong attack to slam the armament down.
skill.attack_type: Strike, Standard and Weapon's Primary Damage Type

weapons.description:
Greatsword embedded with a blue glintstone. Weapon of the trolls in service to the royal family of Caria.

Called into service when the Queen invoked an oath they swore, the trolls are treated as true knights of Caria, and fight arm in arm with their human comrades.

details: Guaranteed drop from the Troll Knight in Carian Manor, just before Royal Knight Loretta, the first time it's killed.

acquisition.location: Caria Manor / Converted Fringe Tower / The Four Belfries
details: 4% drop chance from all Troll Knights.
→ The one in Caria Manor is most easily farmed, in addition to its guaranteed first-time drop of the sword, by starting at the Royal Moongazing Grounds Site of Grace and heading back into the Manor.
→ The spectral Troll Knights at the Four Belfries are also farmable, by starting at either the top or the bottom of the hill.

notes: The Troll Knight's Sword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
The Troll Knight's Sword cannot have its affinities changed with Ashes of War or Whetblades.
The skill, Troll's Roar, is a strong area attack around the user, followed by an overhead slam. Though both of these attacks are slow, they can cause immense Stance damage (76 in total if both land).
→ This sword's version of the skill has strongest scaling and highest possible damage for the initial roar, even compared to a Heavy Affinity weapon, due to the strong base Strength-scaling.

Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack in each two-attack chain is replaced by a thrust. This trait is shared with the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Moonrithyll's Knight Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, and Zweihander.
→ This gives the weapon the versatility of having a thrust attack besides the crouching light attack.

Scales best with an even split between Strength and Dexterity (883 Attack Power), though a pure Strength build has only 6% less Attack Power (831) in exchange for 15% more initial damage with the skill (1,349 Attack Power vs 1,175 Attack Power).

→ Intelligence is largely useless for this weapon beyond the wielding requirement, due to the low base Magic Attack Power and Intelligence-scaling. Terra Magica can slightly increase the damage it deals, but since the Magic Attack Power is only about a quarter of the total Attack Power the effect is rather weak.

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased damage.

weapons.name: Moonrithyll's Knight Sword
weapons.japanese_name: ムーンリデルの騎士剣 (Mūnrideru no Kishiken)

skill.name: Tremendous Phalanx
skill.description: Skill of the enchanted troll knights. Creates a defensive arch of enormous magic glintblades overhead, which automatically attack nearby foes. Follow up with a strong attack to chain this skill into a lunging thrust.

weapons.description:
Greatsword embedded with a blue glintstone. The favored weapon of the steadfast Carian knight, Moonrithyll.

Moonrithyll was the Twin Moon Knight's chamberlain. She was also a friend to the trolls, who served the royal family, and proudly wielded their weapons as she fought arm in arm with her gargantuan comrades.

details: Moonrithyll's Knight Sword can be obtained after defeating the NPC Moonrithyll, Carian Knight.
→ She's found outside of the chapel halfway on the path between the Castle Ensis Checkpoint and Castle-Lord's Chamber Sites of Grace.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The innate skill, Tremendous Phalanx, is effectively the skill version of Greatblade Phalanx and a larger version of the Skill: Glintblade Phalanx. Like those two, this skill's spectral swords can be prepared before battle to immediately launch when an enemy steps into range.
→ Compared to the Troll Knight's Sword's skill the damage and Stance damage is lower, but it's much more mobile and versatile.

Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack in each two-attack chain is replaced by a thrust. This trait is shared with the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Troll Knight's Sword, and Zweihander.
→ This gives the weapon the versatility of having a thrust attack besides the crouching light attack.
Scales best with an even split between Strength and Dexterity (883 Attack Power), though a pure Strength or pure Dexterity build has only 6% less Attack Power (831).

→ Intelligence is largely useless for increasing the weapon's damage, but it will slightly strengthen the skill's projectiles: increasing Intelligence to 30 will increase their Attack Power by 6% compared to having 20 Intelligence, while increasing it to 45 will increase Attack Power by 15%.

weapons.name: Royal Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 王家のグレートソード (Ōke no Gurētosōdo)

skill.name: Wolf's Assault
skill.description: Infuse the greatsword with frost, then perform a forward somersault to plunge it into the ground. Then, pull it out to release a cold blast.

weapons.description:
Greatsword decorated in royal Carian Style. Favored weapon of Blaidd the Half-Wolf.

In defiance of the fate he was born to, Blaidd swore to serve no master but Ranni. As proof. the sword was imbued with a cold magic at the moment oath was sworn.

details: Dropped by Blaidd, along with his armor set (except the Black Wolf Mask), when encountered at Ranni's Rise after Ranni the Witch's storyline has been completed. Killing him prior to this will award no items.

notes: The Royal Greatsword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
The Royal Greatsword cannot be buffed or have its affinities altered with Ashes of War or Whetblades.

The innate skill, Unique Skill: Wolf's Assault, is a leaping stab followed by an explosion. Combined with its Super Armor it's useful as an initiating attack, though it has very limited capability of attacking from above as that can cancel the skill.
The Intelligence-scaling is actually slightly stronger than the Strength-scaling despite having the same letter grade. Additionally, it also strengthens the bonus Magic Attack Power of the skill.

→ This means that a pure Intelligence build is the strongest way to build this weapon. However, because scaling values become less effective after reaching 40-50 in a stat and because wielding this weapon already requires a fair investment in Strength, a hybrid Str/Int build has almost as much AR while requiring much fewer Attribute points to do.

→→ With unmentioned stats at the minimum: 80 Strength grants 886 Attack Power (AP) (907 AP if two-handed), 45 Strength and Intelligence grants 905 AP (941 AP if two-handed), and 80 Intelligence grants 911 AP (943 AP).
The weapon itself does not cause Frostbite but both parts of the skill, the stab-jump and the explosion, do cause some build-up (100 on the stab and 60 on the explosion).

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased physical block rate and guard boost of the Colossal Sword, Colossal Weapons, Great Sword, Great Hammer, Great Axe, Great Spear, and Halberd weapon classes.
patch_notes.community_notes: This weapon's guard ratings were significantly increased, from 55/63/44/44/44/42 to 71/63/44/44/44/52.

weapons.name: Grafted Blade Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 剣接ぎの大剣 (Kentsugi no Taiken)

skill.name: Oath of Vengeance
skill.description: Swear an oath upon the greatsword to avenge the clan, temporarily raising all attributes for a certain duration. While the oath's effects are active, poise will also be increased.

weapons.description:
The storied sword of Castle Morne. A revenger's weapon, it is burdened with oceans of anger and regret. One of the legendary armaments.

A lone surviving champion from a country now vanished was so determined to continue fighting that he claimed the swords of an entire clan of warriors.

details: Defeat the Leonine Misbegotten at the end of the castle.

notes: The Grafted Blade Greatsword cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Grafted Blade Greatsword cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.

The Attribute boosts from this weapon's unique skill, Oath of Vengeance, is especially useful early on, as it will boost your durability by increasing your Defense and HP, and also increase your Equip Load by roughly 8.0 (about 5.6 if accounting for the 70% threshold for Medium Load) letting you carry it easier.
→ Curiously the skill is much quicker than the Skill: Endure is when used with Colossal Swords and has a good bit longer duration (5 seconds instead of 3.5 seconds).
This is one of the earliest available Colossal Swords or Weapons and most likely the second acquired after the Zweihander, also found on the Weeping Peninsula.
While the Dexterity scaling is a good bit stronger than expected it will only exceed the benefits of the Strength scaling when the final softcap of 80 (54 if using both hands) Strength is reached.

Do keep in mind that while the bonuses to Strength and Dexterity can increase the damage dealt by this weapon's attacks it cannot be used to meet the one-handed Attribute requirements as the skill itself is not usable without meeting at least the two-handed requirements.

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased physical block rate and guard boost of the Colossal Sword, Colossal Weapons, Great Sword, Great Hammer, Great Axe, Great Spear, and Halberd weapon classes. Increased the damage of Grafted Blade Greatsword.
patch_notes.community_notes: The block rates and guard boost for the Grafted Blade Greatsword went from 64/48/48/48/48/43 to 80/48/48/48/48/53. The base damage for the Grafted Blade Greatsword went from 157 at +0 and 384 at +10 to 162 at +0 and 396 at +10.

weapons.name: Ruins Greatsword

skill.name: Wave of Destruction
skill.description: Raise the sword up high, then strike it against the ground to fire off a wave of gravitational force.

weapons.description:
Originally rubble from a ruin which fell from the sky, this surviving fragment was honed into a weapon. One of the legendary armaments.

The ruin it came from crumbled when struck by a meteorite, as such this weapon harbors its destructive power.

details: Obtained upon defeating the optional Misbegotten Warrior and Crucible Knight duo boss at the Redmane Castle plaza.

→ Do note that this fight is only available whenever the Radahn festival isn't active. If it's currently active it can be deactivated by defeating Starscourge Radahn and talking to Castellan Jerren once more in the chapel just before the lift down to Radahn and then reloading the area, preferably by teleporting to the Chamber Outside the Plaza Site of Grace.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki rule (Ashes of War cannot be applied to weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones)
notes: The Ruins Greatsword cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The innate, Unique Skill: Wave of Destruction is technically a ranged skill but in practice it's quite usable as a melee attack due to its Hyper Armor.
Has semi-unique one- and two-handed charged heavy attacks, where the usual attack is followed by a burst of stone chunks from the weapon's gravity magic.

→ Though both parts of each attack deals damage, they technically have the same amount of damage potential due to having a Colossal Sword's usual Motion Values divided across two attacks. In practice its damage will be slightly lower due to not being as able to overcome Defence.
→ Deals 50% more Stamina damage against guarding opponents than a Colossal Sword's charged heavy attack usually does.
→ These attacks award twice the amount of points towards the Winged Sword Insignias' damage buff due to both hits granting the usual 14 points each separately.

While this weapon scales with both Strength and Intelligence, it is borderline useless to actually invest in the latter anywhere beyond meeting the Attribute requirements. This is because the damage are incredibly minimal to both normal attacks (maxing out at +32 Magic Attack Power with 99 Intelligence if the weapon is upgraded to +10) and because unlike how these sort of weapons scale normally, where Intelligence provides minimal weapon Attack Power bonuses but great skill Attack Power bonuses, both weapon upgrade level and Strength provide far greater bonuses to the skill's Attack Power.

→ If the player meets the requirement for Strength but not for Intelligence, they will not be able to take advantage of Intelligence scaling, but the base damage of the Physical Attack Power will scale as normal, and the Magic Attack Power will not be reduced. This can ironically make it a good weapon for pure Strength builds as they effectively don't lose much damage but not meeting the Intelligence requirement.
Despite the appearance of its effects it does not cause bonus damage to gravity-type enemies (Fallingstar Beasts and such), presumably because it is not extraterrestrial in origin.
This the second shortest of all Colossal Swords, being longer than only the Starscourge Greatsword.

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased physical block rate and guard boost of the Colossal Sword, Colossal Weapons, Great Sword, Great Hammer, Great Axe, Great Spear, and Halberd weapon classes.
patch_notes.community_notes: The guard damage negations for the Ruins Greatsword went from 65/56/50/50/50/45 to 82/56/50/50/50/56.

weapons.name: Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 古隕鉄の大剣 (Kointetsu no Taiken)

skill.name: White Light Charge
skill.description: Summons white light from the crevice in the weapon's ancient meteoric ore, using its power for a charging attack which pierces foes. Additional input causes the light to explode.

weapons.description:
One of the treasures of the ruined forges. Greatsword of ancient meteoric ore, ending in a sharp point.

Fashioned from an excavated shard of an arrowhead that once was a part of the old gods' arsenal. A capable piercing weapon that excels at thrusting attacks.

details: Obtained upon examining the altar of the dungeon.

→ The altar is found on the second level of the dungeon. To reach it, you must pull the lever to make the iron door rise, and use it as a platform to jump across to the second level where the altar is.

notes: The Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.

White Light Charge causes the wielder of the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword to dash forward with great speed. Inputting the Skill button again after the dash will cause the sword to fire off an explosion of white light.
The Arcane-scaling applies to both the Physical and Magic Attack Power.

Has unique one- and two-handed heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, where the first attack in each two-attack chain is replaced by a thrust. This trait is shared with the Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Moonrithyll's Knight Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, the Troll Knight's Sword, and the Zweihander.
→ This gives the weapon the versatility of having a thrust attack besides the crouching light attack.
Makes great use of the Spear Talisman since its moveset consist of many trusting attacks, including its Unique Skill.

→ Do note that the Talisman isn't quite effective as it can be since it only applies to Pierce (i.e Physical) Attack Power, but since that's still usually about 82-86% (depending on Attribute allocation) of the weapon's total Attack Power it's still quite effective.

Effectively scales about equally well with both Strength and Arcane due to the latter's scaling applying to both damage types. Even a pure Arcane build can use this weapon quite well, though the minimum 35 Strength to wield it (only 24 Strength if two-handed) can make it difficult to fit on such a build.

→ To compare: 80 Strength and 19 Arcane (minimum requirement) grants 860 Attack Power (AP) (898 AP if two-handed), 45 Strength and 45 Arcane grants 837 AP (905 AP if two-handed), and 24 Strength (effectively 36 Strength due to the two-handing Strength boost) and 80 Arcane grants 868 AP.
→ The skill scales entirely with the weapon's Attack Power, so Attribute allocation isn't particularly important for using it either.
This is the longest Colossal Sword.

weapons.name: Starscourge Greatsword
weapons.japanese_name: 星砕きの大剣 (Hoshikudaki no Taiken)

skill.name: Starcaller Cry
skill.description: Bring the two swords together and roar into the skies, pulling in enemies with a gravitational wave. Follow up with an additional input to to slam down with gravity-infused swords.

weapons.description:
Curved greatswords of black steel wielded by General Radahn. A pair of weapons decorated with a lion mane motif.

Radahn earned considerable renown as the Starscourge in his youth, and it is said that it was during this time he engraved the gravity crest upon these blades.

details: Trade the Remembrance of the Starscourge, gained by defeating the Starscourge Radahn, with Finger Reader Enia.
→ Alternatively, use one of the belled Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

notes: Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
Cannot be buffed or infused with Ashes of War.

The Unique Skill: Starcaller Cry is essentially a superpowered version of the Skill: Gravitas, able to pull enemies in and then use an empowered heavy attack as a follow-up to smash them into the ground.
Has a 30% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.

Scales best with Strength until it reaches 54, whereafter Dexterity-scaling becomes equally strong until it the former reaches 80 or the latter reaches 40. Intelligence-scaling is mostly irrelevant for weapon damage.
Despite being paired weapon it still receives the 50% Strength-bonus from two-handing.

→ Note that it doesn't get the usual two-handed bonus to Stance damage. In fact, the Stance damage from the two-handed dual-wield attacks is weaker than the Stance damage of the one-handed light attacks (5.4+5.4 vs 14.4). However, the two-handed jumping dual-wield attacks deal an unusually large amount of Stance damage (10.8+10.8 vs 18.72).
Average weight for a Colossal Sword, effectively allowing dual-wielding with half the weight and therefore with much less required Endurance.
Two-handing replaces the light attack, including all its derivatives, with dual-wield attacks. Blocking also becomes available while heavy attacks remain the same.

Weapon once wielded by Commander Gaius. A combination of greatsword and lance.

Weighty and capable of being brought to bear with great force, this armament shows its true potential when used astride a mount. Gaius himself was never without his boar.

notes: The Sword Lance's pre-equipped skill, Spinning Gravity Thrust, causes the wielder to use gravitational magic to elevate themselves into the air for a brief period, and then preform a corkscrew as they charge forward.
The Sword Lance has the standard light attacks shared by all Heavy Thrusting Swords, however, all the heavy attacks are shared with the Lance, including the Guard Counter.
→ Due to this, the Sword Lance does not have a feint attack like the other Heavy Thrusting Swords as the Great Spear moveset does not have access to those.

The Sword Lance receives an Attack Power boost of 6.4%, 3.7%, and 8.8% respectively with its light attacks, heavy attacks, and charged heavy attacks while riding Torrent, compared to other Heavy Thrusting Swords.

With Heavy Affinity this weapon has a combination of high base Attack Power and very high Strength-scaling, giving it extremely high total Attack Power. This in fact slightly outclasses its Fire Affinity which also has its total Attack Power split between two damage types.

When infused with Cold, Blood, or Poison, the Sword Lance will have much higher status build-up values of those in the same weapon class all while keeping respectable Strength-scaling. When combined with Spinning Gravity Thrust, the Sword Lance is capable of inflicting status aliments quickly and consistently.
→ More specifically, the Status Effect build-up is on par with a Colossal Sword's build-up.

Notably weaker with the Sacred and Flame Art Affinities, as it has comparatively much stronger Strength-scaling but 30% weaker Faith-scaling. This is just enough to make it the weakest Heavy Thrusting Sword on these Affinities.
The Sword Lance is the only Legendary armament that can be infused with Ashes of War, be buffed by spells or consumables, and is upgraded by regular Smithing Stones.
→ Despite having Legendary status, it is NOT required for the Legendary Armaments trophy and achievement.

Strength is the Attribute that scales the weapon's overall Attack Power the best, though adding some Dexterity and/or Faith to the Strength also works well.
→ More specifically, a pure Strength build, a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, a hybrid Strength/Faith, and a hybrid Strength/Dexterity/Faith build gains roughly equal total Attack Power.

→ The Faith-scaling is the only way to strengthen the Fire Attack Power of both the weapon and the Unique Skill's Magma Pools, which is easier to strengthen than the Physical Attack Power thanks to Buffs like the Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear.

weapons.name: Spirit Sword

skill.name: Rancor Slash
skill.description: Spin around, slashing foes while summoning vengeful spirits which chase down foes. Additional input allows for a follow-up attack.

weapons.description:
Sharp blade sculpted into a twisted shape. A sword that has seen many years of use in the gravesite.

Said to serve as a medium for communion with spirits.

details: This weapon can be found in a triangular ravine behind the stranded coffin boat just northeast of the Cerulean Coast West Site of Grace. It's in the far right corner, near some gravestones and Demi-Humans.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The Unique Skill: Rancor Slash is essentially a variant of the Skill: Sword Dance with added projectiles.
→ Similarly to Sword Dance, this skill is a strong gap-closer and roll-catch, functions which are strengthened by the added projectiles.
→ This skill is the only source of Frostbite on the weapon thanks to the skull projectiles, with the first input inflicting up to 60 build-up and the second input inflicting up to 90 build-up.

While the Dexterity and Intelligence scalings of this weapon are technically equally strong, the Physical Attack Power being higher than the Magic Attack Power means that Dexterity gives greater bonuses than Intelligence.

→ However, since scalings reach their first softcap around 50-55 a pure Dexterity build grants roughly as much Attack Power as a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build with Dexterity that is either equal to or greater than Intelligence. A hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build also has 15-25% higher Attack Power than a pure Dexterity build with the skull projectiles, depending on how much Intelligence one has.
This weapon is quite short.

weapons.name: Nox Flowing Sword
weapons.japanese_name: ノクスの流体剣 (Nokusu no Ryūtaiken)

skill.name: Flowing Form
skill.description: Temporarily transforms armament into its liquid form. Swing the armament like a whip to perform a sweeping slice over a wide area.

weapons.description:
A grim weapon wielded by swordsmen of the Eternal City, this shotel has a blade as fine as a needle.

Forged from the liquid metal of a Silver Tear, it is thoroughly tempered until hardened.

details: Received upon defeating the Nox Swordstress & Nox Monk duo boss in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, just east of the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid.
→ Accessing the duo requires lighting the three braziers in the town to remove a seal.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki rule (Ashes of War cannot be applied to weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones)

notes: The Unique Skill: Flowing Form functions as a crowd control attack, giving this Curved Sword a good tool for handling groups of enemies while also having decent stagger power.
All attacks ignore at least 50% of a blocking opponents Guarded Damage Negation.
→ Heavy attacks and feint attacks ignore 70% of Guarded Damage Negation, and charged heavy attacks ignore 80% of Guarded Damage Negation.

→ The feint attack becomes an excellent tool against parries thanks to this due to being unparryable and initially very similar to the charged heavy attack, making it easier to bait out a parry that can simply be pierced through.
Has unique, more horizontal heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks, and the charged heavy attacks also only hit once. Shared with the Shotel and Eclipse Shotel.

→ The heavy attacks are effectively pretty much identical to those of other Curved Swords, but the charged heavy attacks sacrifice a bit of the ability to gain boosts from the Winged Sword Insignias in exchange for taking about half a second less to perform per attack.
This is one of the longest Curved Swords, and the longest of all shotels by a fair bit.
Does best with a pure Dexterity build, though a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build is only about 8% weaker after Dexterity hits 50 or so.

→ The total Attack Power is about average compared to a Keen Affinity Curved Sword with a pure Dexterity build, though this is in the context of it not being buffable and it being the stronger alternative to the Shotel on this Affinity.

patch_notes.official_notes: Increased guard penetration
patch_notes.community_notes: Increased the base amount of ignored Guarded Damage Negation per attack from 40% to 50%. Also applied to a variety of other guard-piercing weapons.

weapons.name: Wing of Astel
weapons.japanese_name: アステールの薄羽 (Asutēru no Usuba)

skill.name: Nebula
skill.description: Imbue the Naturalborn's wings with magic to send forth a dark cloud of stars that lingers briefly before exploding.

weapons.description:
Sword fashioned from a delicate wing, suffused with the magic of the stars. Strong attack unleashes a wave of enchanted light.

Crafted from a relic of the Naturalborn of the Void who is said to have assailed the Eternal City.

details: Found inside a chest in Uhl Palace Ruins above a Malformed Star, located in Ainsel River and only reachable from Ainsel River Main. More specifically, start from Ainsel River Main Site of Grace and head down the tunnel. Take the left split in the road, guarded by a Hardhead Giant Ant, and follow the cliffside path to a stone structure with the chest.

notes: The Wing of Astel cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Wing of Astel cannot have its Ash of War or Affinity changed.

The Unique Skill: Nebula is a series of explosive Magic bursts, which can be bunched up in enclosed spaces. Used right next to an enemy or while aimed down at the ground it will deal heavy area damage.
→ This weapon's variant of Nebula is different from the one Bastard's Stars, being a close-ranged burst of explosions instead of a lunging swing followed by explosions.
Has a +20% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.

Standing regular and charged heavy attacks also throws out one and two Magic beams respectively, in addition to the normal parts of a heavy attack. Since both parts can hit the same enemy, this weapon deals greatly increase damage and Stance damage on hit, at no FP cost.

→ Each of these projectiles deal extra Stance damage in addition to the regular Stance damage of these attacks. It won't be that much at range, but in melee that will increase the Stance damage of standing heavy attacks by 50% and of charged heavy attacks by 33%.
The skill's damage is increased by Spellblade's Set (though not the heavy attack beams).

weapons.name: Falx

skill.name: Revenger's Blade
skill.description: Dash up to an enemy and slash them open with the blades held in each hand. By holding down the button, the initial dash will be extended. Follow up with strong attack to hack the enemy to pieces.

weapons.description:
Curved swords with long sickle-like blades. A pair of weapons made to be wielded in both hands

Forged by a hornsent in the name of revenge. "In vengeance for the flames, my blade I wield..."

acquisition.location: Shadow Keep / Ancient Ruins of Rauh / Enir-Ilim
details: The Falx is a guaranteed drop depending on how the player interacts with Hornsent after Miquella's Great Rune breaks.
→ If the player summons Hornsent to help defeat Messmer the Impaler, he will invade as a hostile NPC near the Rauh Ancient Ruins Site of Grace. He will drop the Falx upon his defeat.
→ If the player sides with Needle Knight Leda in invading Hornsent, he will drop his weapon upon his defeat.
→ If the Hornsent is left alive and assists Needle Knight Leda during her boss fight, the Falx will be found on his corpse after the player wins the fight.

notes: The Falx cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Falx cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.
The Unique Skill: Revenger's Blade is a strong attack with good Hyper Armor, and since it includes a dash it can be used for engaging enemies during an opening.
→ The strong attack follow-up to it is also a good roll-catch, due to its good turning ability and having a short lunge.
This is a Paired Weapon, meaning that trying to two-hand it will instead pull out a second Falx.

Though doesn't have a lot of Blood Loss build-up, the fact that it's a paired weapon and the multi-hit nature of the skill's follow-up attack means that it can still inflict the Status Effect decently well.
The weapon scales primarily with Dexterity but can still gain some benefit from Strength, especially after reaching 80 Dexterity.

patch_notes.official_notes: Fixed a bug where the power of some Weapon Skills of a right-handed Falx changed depending on the level of the weapon equipped in the left hand.

weapons.name: Dancing Blade of Ranah
weapons.japanese_name: ラーナの舞踏剣 (Rāna no Butōken)

skill.name: Unending Dance
skill.description: A furious dance formed by a succession of slashing attacks. Hold the button down to sustain the dance for as long as stamina allows.

weapons.description:
Decorative swords ablaze with impassioned red. A pair of weapons made to be wielded in both hands.

Used by the dancers of Ranah. Strike enemies with a dancing assault when executing a strong attack.

details: Dropped by the Dancer of Ranah, found inside of the Southern Nameless Mausoleum.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The Unique Skill: Unending Dance is a series of sword slashes in the form of a graceful dance. Holding down the Skill button extends the dance for as long as the user has Stamina.
The Attack Power of the heavy attacks and the skill, Unending Dance, are boosted by wearing pieces of the Dancer's Set.
Scales purely from Dexterity and has a minimal Strength requirement, making this weapon a great choice for pure Dexterity builds.
This weapon has unique, dance-like heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks that hit twice instead of once and thrice instead of twice respectively. This is shared with the Flowing Curved Sword.

→ These are slightly slower than regular Curved Sword heavy attacks and charged heavy attacks but grant more points towards the Winged Sword Insignias (20 points instead of 10 points for the heavy attacks and 30 points instead of 20 points for the charged heavy attacks).
→ These unique heavy attacks receive a +2.5% Damage Boost for each piece of the Dancer's Set Shadow of the Erdtree that is worn (+10.4% for the whole set).
The Dancing Blade of Ranah is a Paired Weapon; two-handing the sword will cause the player to equip a second sword in their off-hand.

weapons.name: Horned Warrior's Sword
weapons.japanese_name: 角の戦士の曲剣 (Tsuno no Senshi no Kyokken)

skill.name: Horn Calling
skill.description: Invokes tangled horns to cover the weapon's blade. Drive the weapon into the ground, calling up a cluster of piercing horns.

weapons.description:
Curved sword of the horned warriors, keepers of the tower.

The ornamental tangled horns allow the blade to serve as a medium for horn-calling.

acquisition.location: Belurat, Tower Settlement / Rauh Base / Midra's Manse / Ancient Ruins of Rauh
details: 4% drop rate from dual-wielding Horned Warriors.
→ One can be found in the Belurat Tower Settlement Swamp.
→ An easy one to farm is located just up the stairs from the Small Private Altar Site of Grace in Belurat, Tower Settlement.
→ Another is located just by the Ravine North Site of Grace in Rauh Base.

upgrade.changeability_info_source: wiki (Ash of War-Compatible Armaments) + deduced (affinity_changeable: wiki rule, a weapon upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones takes no Ash of War, hence no affinity)

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The Unique Skill: Horn Calling is a strong, Holy ranged attack, useful for this rather short weapon.
The Horned Warrior's Sword is a Paired Weapon; two-handing the sword will cause the player to equip a second sword in their off-hand.
Unusually, this weapon's Physical Attack Power scales with not only Strength and Dexterity, but also Faith.
